guide.title: Steakhouses in Los Angeles: Twelve in the City, Six Over the Line
guide.intro: Eighteen rooms on this page across three municipalities, because the beef in this city does not stop at a boundary sign. Twelve stand in the City of Los Angeles: two on the Koreatown grid at Sixth and Eighth Streets, an Argentine grill in the Arts District, a wagyu room on the second floor of the Wilshire Grand, a butcher's bar in Echo Park, four along the Melrose and Sunset corridor from Larchmont to Hollywood, one on Washington Boulevard in Venice and two on Ventura Boulevard in the Valley. Five more sit in Beverly Hills, on Wilshire, Canon Drive, Beverly Drive and La Cienega. One holds Sunset Boulevard in West Hollywood. Each room carries the node of the city it is actually in, so a Beverly Hills address files under Beverly Hills even though it is published here.

sections.heading: Koreatown and Downtown
sections.body:
Five rooms on the flat middle of the city, and no two of them are the same genre.

Woo Hyang Woo is on West Sixth Street in Koreatown, a Korean beef barbecue room working USDA Prime, wagyu and Certified Angus beef, with tomahawk short ribs as the signature. Taylor's Steakhouse is nine blocks south at Eighth and Ardmore, an old-world dining room the Taylor family moved to in 1970, according to the restaurant's own history, and still runs.

Malbec is on Traction Avenue in the Arts District, an Argentine kitchen with the tomahawk on a long menu of grilled beef and empanadas. Niku X occupies the second floor of the Wilshire Grand Center at 900 Wilshire Boulevard — certified Japanese A5 wagyu, chef Shin Thompson, and a public entrance with no ticket or admission required to reach it. Butchr Bar is the outlier, an Australian-owned room on Glendale Boulevard in Echo Park where lamb, Australian wagyu and cured boar hang in lit dry-aging chambers behind the counter and grass-fed wagyu steaks come off the grill in front of it.

sections.heading: Melrose, Sunset and Larchmont
sections.body:
Four rooms on the Hollywood side of the city, three of them on the same avenue.

Chi Spacca is at 6610 Melrose Avenue, Nancy Silverton's meat room in the Mozza group, where a fifty-ounce bistecca fiorentina is the centerpiece of the menu. Kali Steak is further east at 5722 Melrose; it closed in January 2025 for a remodel and reopened that July with the tasting menu gone and an à la carte steakhouse list in its place, chef Kevin Meehan still in the kitchen. Carlitos Gardel is west at 7963 Melrose, a family-run Argentine steakhouse with a heated patio called Patio Piazzolla and a Plate distinction from the Michelin Guide. Beverly Grove is City of Los Angeles ground, whatever the surrounding street names suggest.

Gwen is around the corner at 6600 Sunset Boulevard, an old-world European butcher shop and a Michelin-starred dining room under the same roof, cooking dry-aged steaks over fire. Chef Curtis Stone runs it.

sections.heading: Venice and the Valley
sections.body:
Three rooms at the far edges of the city, one at the ocean and two over the hill.

Charcoal Venice is on Washington Boulevard, which its own kitchen describes as part steakhouse and part backyard barbecue: everything is cooked indoors over live fire, whether over charcoal or down in the coals, and a forty-eight-ounce dry-aged porterhouse is the large-format cut. Josiah Citrin owns it.

Over the Cahuenga Pass, Ventura Boulevard carries two. Alto is in Studio City, a South American steakhouse built around an open grill. BLVD Steak is in Sherman Oaks on the restaurant row stretch, where prime cuts and seafood are what the menu is founded on. Both addresses are inside the City of Los Angeles.

sections.heading: Beverly Hills and West Hollywood
sections.body:
Six rooms outside the city line but inside the page, because the beef culture here runs across all three municipalities.

CUT is inside the Beverly Wilshire at 9500 Wilshire Boulevard, Wolfgang Puck's steak room in a 104-seat all-white dining room designed by Richard Meier; Michelin awarded it a star in 2019 and again in 2021. Steak 48 opened at 9680 Wilshire in January 2023. Mastro's holds 246 North Canon Drive, with the Penthouse on the third floor reached by its own lift, a terrace and a DJ every night. Matū is on South Beverly Drive and does one thing: 100% grass-fed wagyu from First Light Farms in New Zealand, served as a sequence of cuts. Lawry's The Prime Rib is on North La Cienega Boulevard, where prime rib is carved at your table from silver carts that Lawrence Frank designed — five feet long and six hundred pounds each.

West Hollywood's one room is BOA Steakhouse at 9200 Sunset Boulevard, working a dry-aged New York strip, a bone-in rib eye and A5 Japanese wagyu.

faq.question: Why does a Los Angeles page cover Beverly Hills and West Hollywood?
faq.answer: Because the beef culture spans the municipalities and the City of Los Angeles sustains the page on its own. Twelve rooms sit inside the city limits, so Beverly Hills and West Hollywood are additions rather than a crutch. Each room still carries the node of the city it is actually in: CUT files under Beverly Hills, BOA under West Hollywood, and Carlitos Gardel under Los Angeles because Beverly Grove is City of Los Angeles ground.

faq.question: What makes a room a steakhouse on this page?
faq.answer: Steak has to be the menu's center of gravity, plus the beef-centric genres — churrascaria, Argentine parrilla, Japanese wagyu counter, Korean-style beef room. That line keeps three well-regarded rooms off the list. Dan Tana's in West Hollywood is an Italian restaurant whose menu revolves around pasta, veal and seafood, however famous its New York steak is. Vaca in Downtown is a Spanish restaurant built on tapas, paella and jamón. Dunsmoor in Glassell Park is an American heritage kitchen of oysters, cornbread and pork chops with one very good ribeye on it. A restaurant that merely serves a good steak is out.

faq.question: Which rooms did this survey find closed?
faq.answer: Two. Nusr-Et closed its Beverly Hills room on 4 June 2025 as the chain withdrew from most of the United States. Wolfgang's Steakhouse on North Canon Drive no longer appears on its own operator's list of locations, which now runs New York, New Jersey, Waikiki and a set of international rooms with nothing in California. Neither is published here.

faq.question: Do the Argentine and Korean rooms count as steakhouses?
faq.answer: Yes. The rule names them: churrascaria, Argentine parrilla, Japanese wagyu counter and Korean-style beef room are all in, because in this city the beef culture genuinely is those genres as much as it is the chophouse. Malbec and Carlitos Gardel are Argentine, Woo Hyang Woo is a Korean beef room, Niku X and Matū are wagyu rooms, and none of them is a guest on this page.

faq.question: Why is Smith & Wollensky not listed in Century City?
faq.answer: Because it is not there. The operator's own list of locations runs Boston, Wellesley, Chicago, Las Vegas, Miami Beach, New York and a set of international rooms, with no Los Angeles site on it. An earlier draft of this survey carried one; the check removed it.

photos.title: Wilshire Boulevard looking west toward Beverly Hills
photos.description: An empty six-lane roadway running away from the camera under a pale morning sky, a mirrored office tower and a pink granite one on the left, a blue-glass tower and a low brick building numbered 6435 on the right, and palms and lamp-post banners lining both curbs. Wilshire Boulevard in the Fairfax District, looking west toward Beverly Hills.
photos.author: Downtowngal

places.name: Woo Hyang Woo
places.summary: Woo Hyang Woo is a Korean beef barbecue room on West Sixth Street in Koreatown. The house works USDA Prime, wagyu and Certified Angus beef, and the tomahawk short ribs are the signature cut.

places.name: Taylor's Steakhouse
places.summary: Taylor's is an old-world steakhouse at Eighth Street and Ardmore Avenue, on the Koreatown edge of Mid-Wilshire. There is a full bar, a private group room, and a menu that has not chased anything in decades.
places.history: The Taylor family moved the restaurant to this corner in 1970, according to the restaurant's own history, and the founders' son took it over in 1978.

places.name: Malbec
places.summary: Malbec is an Argentine grill on Traction Avenue in the Arts District. The tomahawk anchors a long menu of grilled beef, seafood rice dishes and empanadas.

places.name: Butchr Bar
places.summary: Butchr Bar is an Australian-owned butchery and restaurant on Glendale Boulevard in Echo Park. Lamb, Australian wagyu and cured boar hang in lit dry-aging chambers, and grass-fed wagyu steaks and house-made charcuterie come off the counter in front of them.

places.name: Niku X
places.address: 900 Wilshire Blvd, 2nd Floor, Los Angeles, CA 90017
places.summary: Niku X is a Japanese steakhouse on the second floor of the Wilshire Grand Center in Downtown Los Angeles, built on certified Japanese A5 wagyu under chef Shin Thompson. It has its own entrance and its own reservation line, and no ticket or admission is required to reach it from the street.

places.name: Chi Spacca
places.summary: Chi Spacca is Nancy Silverton's beef and butchery room on Melrose Avenue, the meat end of the Mozza group. A fifty-ounce bistecca fiorentina — a Tuscan porterhouse cut for a table — is the centerpiece of the menu and the clearest statement of what the kitchen does with fire.

places.name: Gwen
places.summary: Gwen is chef Curtis Stone's Hollywood room on Sunset Boulevard: an old-world, European-style butcher shop at the front and a Michelin-starred dining room behind it. Dry-aged steaks come off a menu built on fire-based cooking.

places.name: Kali Steak
places.summary: Kali Steak is chef Kevin Meehan's room on Melrose Avenue near Larchmont. It closed in January 2025 for a remodel and reopened that July with the tasting menu dropped and an à la carte mid-century steakhouse list in its place — steaks, a wedge salad, Parker House rolls.

places.name: Carlitos Gardel
places.summary: Carlitos Gardel is a family-run Argentine steakhouse on Melrose Avenue in Beverly Grove, which is City of Los Angeles ground rather than Beverly Hills. There is a formal dining room and a covered, heated patio called Patio Piazzolla, and the Michelin Guide lists the room with a Plate distinction.

places.name: Alto
places.summary: Alto is a South American steakhouse on Ventura Boulevard in Studio City, built around an open grill that does the dramatic work at the front of the room.

places.name: BLVD Steak
places.summary: BLVD Steak sits on the restaurant row stretch of Ventura Boulevard in Sherman Oaks. Prime cuts and fresh seafood are the foundation of the menu, with an international wine list beside them.

places.name: Charcoal Venice
places.summary: Charcoal is Josiah Citrin's Washington Boulevard room in Venice, which the kitchen calls part steakhouse and part backyard barbecue. Everything is cooked indoors over live fire, whether over charcoal or down in the coals, and a forty-eight-ounce dry-aged porterhouse is the large-format cut.

places.name: CUT by Wolfgang Puck
places.summary: CUT is Wolfgang Puck's steak room inside the Beverly Wilshire on Wilshire Boulevard, a 104-seat all-white dining room designed by Richard Meier. Premium cuts of beef and Japanese wagyu are the menu; Michelin awarded the room a star in 2019 and again in 2021.

places.name: Mastro's Steakhouse
places.address: 246 N Canon Dr, Beverly Hills, CA 90210
places.summary: Mastro's Beverly Hills is a two-level steakhouse on North Canon Drive with the Penthouse above it on the third floor, reached by its own lift. The signature cuts and iced seafood towers are downstairs; the terrace, the sushi list and a nightly DJ are up top.

places.name: Lawry's The Prime Rib
places.address: 100 N La Cienega Blvd, Beverly Hills, CA 90211
places.summary: Lawry's is a prime rib room on North La Cienega Boulevard where roasts of beef are carved at your table by a master carver working from a silver cart. Lawrence Frank designed the carts himself: five feet long and six hundred pounds apiece.

places.name: Steak 48
places.summary: Steak 48's Beverly Hills room opened on Wilshire Boulevard in January 2023. USDA Prime steaks and Wagyu come out of a glass-walled show kitchen, with a raw bar and seafood beside them.

places.name: Matū
places.address: 239 S Beverly Dr, Suite 100, Beverly Hills, CA 90212
places.summary: Matū is a beef room on South Beverly Drive with a single source: 100% grass-fed wagyu from First Light Farms in New Zealand. The menu runs as a sequence of cuts and preparations rather than a list of steaks, and the Michelin Guide lists it.

places.name: BOA Steakhouse
places.summary: BOA holds the Sunset Strip corner at 9200 Sunset Boulevard in West Hollywood. The list runs a 40-day dry-aged New York strip, according to the restaurant's own menu, alongside a bone-in rib eye, certified organic beef and A5 Japanese wagyu.

entries.name: Woo Hyang Woo
entries.note: West Sixth Street, Koreatown. Order the tomahawk short ribs; this is a beef room before it is a barbecue room.

entries.name: Taylor's Steakhouse
entries.note: Eighth Street at Ardmore. An old-world dining room, and the family that moved it here is still running it.

entries.name: Malbec
entries.note: Traction Avenue, Arts District. The Argentine end of downtown, and the tomahawk is the reason to go.

entries.name: Butchr Bar
entries.note: Glendale Boulevard, Echo Park. Look at the aging chambers before you order; the wagyu is grass-fed.

entries.name: Niku X
entries.note: Second floor of the Wilshire Grand. A5 wagyu downtown, and you walk in off Wilshire without a ticket.

entries.name: Chi Spacca
entries.note: 6610 Melrose Avenue. The fifty-ounce bistecca is sized for a table, not a person.

entries.name: Gwen
entries.note: 6600 Sunset Boulevard. Buy beef at the butcher counter on the way past, or sit down behind it.

entries.name: Kali Steak
entries.note: 5722 Melrose Avenue. The steakhouse it became in July 2025, not the tasting-menu room it was before.

entries.name: Carlitos Gardel
entries.note: 7963 Melrose Avenue. Beverly Grove, not Beverly Hills — and the heated patio is the seat to ask for.

entries.name: Alto
entries.note: Ventura Boulevard, Studio City. The open grill is the show, and the Valley's half of this page starts here.

entries.name: BLVD Steak
entries.note: Ventura Boulevard, Sherman Oaks. Restaurant row, prime cuts, and a wine list that travels.

entries.name: Charcoal Venice
entries.note: Washington Boulevard, Venice. Everything is cooked over live fire indoors; the porterhouse is the large format.

entries.name: CUT by Wolfgang Puck
entries.note: Inside the Beverly Wilshire. A Richard Meier dining room and a Michelin star to go with the beef.

entries.name: Mastro's Steakhouse
entries.note: North Canon Drive. The Penthouse on the third floor is a different room from the steakhouse below it.

entries.name: Lawry's The Prime Rib
entries.note: North La Cienega Boulevard. The silver cart comes to the table and the carving happens in front of you.

entries.name: Steak 48
entries.note: 9680 Wilshire Boulevard. The newest of the Beverly Hills five, open since January 2023.

entries.name: Matū
entries.note: South Beverly Drive. One farm, one breed, and the menu reads as a sequence of cuts.

entries.name: BOA Steakhouse
entries.note: 9200 Sunset Boulevard. The one West Hollywood room on this page, at the Strip end of Sunset.
